evidence: bp-service.lisp:610-615 `(fnn-store-fault (e) (error e)) ((or fnn-os-error sb-bsd-sockets:socket-error fnn-store-error) () (setq outcome (if socket :uncertain :failed)))`. fnn-store-indeterminate is a subtype of fnn-store-error (io.lisp:92), so it lands in the transport branch. Also, line 582 `(setq socket nil)` runs before the fragment loop (587-608), whose inner handler catches only os and socket errors. The comment at 584-586 says "after the first fragment has gone a connect that sent nothing is :uncertain, never :failed".
fix: Add an explicit `(fnn-store-indeterminate (e) (error e))` arm before the fnn-store-error arm. Track "any octet sent" with its own flag set before the fragment loop, rather than reusing `socket`.
reviewer: bp-service.lisp:610-615: fnn-store-fault is re-signalled, but fnn-store-indeterminate (a subtype of fnn-store-error, io.lisp:92) is caught by the transport branch and becomes :uncertain/:failed. The only realistic indeterminate source inside this session is finding 2's stray inbound staging (tcpcl.lisp:273), so (a) needs a misbehaving peer plus EIO, and it fences a file nothing reads. (b) is real: socket is set to nil at line 582 before the fragment loop. The inner handler (606-607) catches only os and socket errors, so a store-error in fragment session 2 or later reaches the outer handler. That handler sets :failed and skips fn-bpfs-fragment-outcome, the function that turns a later fragment's :failed into :uncertain (books/bp-fragment-send.lisp:1308-1310). The trigger for (b) is narrow, because params are unchanged across fragment sessions.
scenario: (a) During the send session the peer offers a transfer. fnn-tcl-stage's barrier fails and raises fnn-indeterminate. That becomes the transport outcome :uncertain, the machine requeues the job and keeps publishing, and the ambiguous persistence failure is lost. (b) The first fragment is accepted, then fragment 2's session raises any fnn-store-error (for example `tcpcl: the session machine refused these parameters`, or the indeterminate above). socket is already nil, so outcome becomes :failed ("certainly did not happen") for a job whose first fragment was delivered.
title: bp-service send path reports an indeterminate publication as transport :uncertain/:failed, and reports :failed after fragments were sent
